redesigned_cot:
CHOSEN APPROACH (of 3 considered): "Full fixed table-walk with printed value table." Rejected alt A = "terse current style + add inline val anchor" (still skips rows, row-jump stays regime-3). Rejected alt B = "hard-code 100 memorized n->Roman lookup lines" (zero generalization, pure memorization, collapses on the test n that wasn't a training mode = textbook regime-3). Chosen design makes the next row POSITIONALLY DETERMINISTIC (always the next of 9 fixed table entries) and makes every value+symbol a COPY from a value table printed verbatim above. EXACT SKELETON (one helper formats every line byte-identically; lines indented with two spaces; " : ", " >= ", " < ", " - ", " = " separators are behavioral and fixed):

Line 1: `This is an Arabic to Roman numeral conversion.`
Line 2: (blank)
Line 3 (R2 ANCHOR, restate input verbatim): `Input number: {n}`
Line 4: (blank)
Line 5: `Value table (largest to smallest):`
Lines 6-14 (R5 FIXED BLOCK, byte-identical in EVERY trace, all 9 rows always, in this order):
`  C = 100`
`  XC = 90`
`  L = 50`
`  XL = 40`
`  X = 10`
`  IX = 9`
`  V = 5`
`  IV = 4`
`  I = 1`
Line 15: (blank)
Line 16: `Greedy subtraction from {n}:`
Reduction region (R3 ONE MICRO-STEP PER LINE, R1 full table walk): iterate the 9 table rows IN FIXED ORDER. For each row (value v, symbol s): WHILE running_remainder >= v emit a TAKE line, then emit exactly one SKIP line when the row is exhausted. Two and only two line templates:
  TAKE: `  {r} >= {v} : take {s}, {r} - {v} = {new}`
  SKIP: `  {r} < {v} : skip {s}`
where {r} = current running remainder (copied = the {new} of the previous line, or {n} for the first line), {v} and {s} are COPIED from the value table above, {new} = r - v (single-digit-domain local subtraction, r<=100). Every one of the 9 rows always contributes at least its SKIP line, so the walk is uniform and the position deterministically keys the next (v,s) pair. (n=4 example body: skip C, skip XC, skip L, skip XL, skip X, skip IX, skip V, take IV 4-4=0, skip IV, skip I. n=88 body: skip C, skip XC, take L 88-50=38, skip L, skip XL, take X 38-10=28, take X 28-10=18, take X 18-10=8, skip X, skip IX, take V 8-5=3, skip V, skip IV, take I 3-1=2, take I 2-1=1, take I 1-1=0, skip I.)
blank line
(R6 incremental assembly, each on its own line): `Symbols taken in order: {s1} {s2} ... {sk}` (space-joined, copies of the take lines' symbols in order; `(none)` only if empty, which never happens for n>=1)
`Concatenate: {s1s2...sk}` (the same symbols with no spaces — the literal answer string)
blank line
`The answer is \boxed{{{joined}}}` where {joined} is a CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER copy of the `Concatenate:` line value directly above.

The completion is wrapped exactly as the pinned category template `<think>\n{cot}\n</think>\n\boxed{{{ans}}}<|im_end|>` (R5 format identity).

AUGMENTERS (R8, empty-<think> drills in IDENTICAL surface format, category-tagged, deterministic selection a la matching.py): (1) value-table-copy drill: prompt gives a value e.g. `XL = ?` or `? = 40`, completion is the table line — drills the val<->sym copy primitive. (2) single-subtraction drill: prompt `r - v = ?` for the exact `{r} - {v} = {new}` surface, r in 1..100 — drills the one local subtraction. (3) symbol-concatenate drill: prompt the `Symbols taken in order: L X X X V I I I` line, completion the `Concatenate: LXXXVIII` line — drills the space-strip/concat copy that produces the boxed string. All use enable_thinking=False and the same chat template; validate mod_used>0.
oracle_preservation_argument: The redesigned CoT computes the answer with the SAME greedy-subtraction algorithm as src/reasoners/numeral.py (identical ROMAN value list, restricted to the 1..100 symbols that ever occur), so the assembled `Concatenate:` string equals _to_roman(n) by construction. I ran an offline check (/tmp/numeral_redesign_check.py) generating the redesigned trace for ALL n in 1..100 and comparing the boxed answer to ''.join(_to_roman(n)): result 'all answers correct (oracle preserved): True, mismatches: 0'. The audit (/tmp/numeral_audit.py) additionally verified box == `Concatenate:` line == oracle answer for all 100 n. NOTE: my first draft used an `if` instead of a `while` per table row and the offline check immediately caught 65 mismatches (e.g. n=88 -> LXIXVIVI instead of LXXXVIII) — fixing the row to fire while r>=v made all 100 correct, which is exactly why the offline check is mandatory. Grader-wise the boxed value is a self-consistent copy of the trace's own computation and metric_correct does case-insensitive string-exact on Roman strings, so the grader-correct answer is reproduced.
offline_validation: Run `python3 /tmp/numeral_redesign_check.py` (regenerable; logic mirrors src/reasoners/numeral.py with the 1..100 symbol subset). It asserts three things over n=1..100: (1) ORACLE PRESERVED — boxed answer == ''.join(_to_roman(n)) for every n (prints 'all answers correct: True, mismatches: 0'); (2) UNDER CAP — wraps each trace in the pinned `<think>...</think>\\boxed{}<|im_end|>` template, tokenizes with src/tokenizer.json, reports max completion tokens = 408 at n=88 (< 7680). Then run `python3 /tmp/numeral_audit.py` for TEMPLATE UNIFORMITY + R-safety: byte-deterministic across two runs (True); every compute line matches one of exactly two regexes TAKE `^  \\d+ >= \\d+ : take [A-Z]+, \\d+ - \\d+ = \\d+$` or SKIP `^  \\d+ < \\d+ : skip [A-Z]+$`, plus the 9 fixed table rows — 0 violations; locality (left operand of every line == running remainder) True; box == Concatenate line == oracle True. Before any paid run, also grep the generated reasoning/*.txt for global-rule phrasings ('the rule is','pattern is','shift') — none should appear; and confirm the 9-row Value table block is byte-identical across sampled traces (diff two traces: only the `Input number`, the reduction body, and the answer slots may differ).

verdict_fixes.counterexample: none found after honest effort. Verified all n in 1..100 (the proven exact corpus range) and all 1576 real corpus numeral problems: the redesigned CoT's boxed answer equals _to_roman(n) and passes the grader (metric_correct + extract_answer) in every case, 0 mismatches. n=100 (claimed max, 11 occurrences) correctly yields C. The only breakage is for inputs n>=400 (e.g. 400 -> CCCC instead of CD, 1000 -> ten C's instead of M) because the table is restricted to <=100 symbols, but I confirmed (by inverting all 1576 stored Roman answers) that the corpus max is exactly 100 and zero inputs are >=400, so no real corpus instance is ever mishandled. This is a robustness gap on inputs that never occur, not an oracle regression.
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: No fix needed for the corpus (range 1..100, oracle preserved on all 1576 problems). Optional defensive hardening only if the unseen test distribution could exceed 100: restore the full 13-row ROMAN table (add M/CM/D/CD rows in fixed order) so the table-walk stays correct for n up to 3999. This is purely belt-and-suspenders; it does not affect any corpus instance and adds 4 always-skip rows per trace (still far under the 7680 cap). Keep the WHILE-per-row (not IF) loop, which the spec already verified is mandatory.

verdict_fixes.counterexample: none found after honest effort. Full-prefix divergence audit over all completion tokens of n=1..100 found exactly ONE branch point (`Input number: ` -> n), where n is a regime-1 copy from the prompt; all 0 other divergences. Every downstream committed token (v, s, op, new, taken-symbols, concatenate, box) is a deterministic single-valued function of tokens already printed in the same completion. The redesign correctly BOXES the trace's own computed value (box == Concatenate line == oracle for all 100 n). No step requires inferring a per-item GLOBAL rule; the legacy regime-3 hazard (9-mode row-jump after `{n} >= ` because non-taken rows were skipped, so position did not key the table row) is eliminated by the uniform 9-row walk + value-table anchor. No over-cap risk (worst case n=88 = ~396-408 tokens vs 7680 cap).
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: No blocking fix required; the design is R-safe and oracle-preserving (verified offline: 0/100 mismatches vs ''.join(_to_roman(n))). OPTIONAL hardening if a future paid run still under-performs: (1) to fully satisfy R3 purism, split each 2-digit subtraction into tens/ones digit lines -- but this is likely unnecessary (legacy subtraction never collapsed and adds length/fragility, so do NOT do it pre-emptively). (2) For honest R9 attribution, change ONE variable per paid run: first ship legacy-style + the uniform full-row walk ONLY (the actual fix for the regime-3 row-jump), holding the value-table-anchor and explicit-skip cosmetics constant, so a score move is attributable to the locality fix rather than the bundle. Keep the three drill augmenters (table-copy, single-subtraction, symbol-concatenate) -- they correctly target the only computed primitives.
rubric_violations: R3 / antipattern-6 (minor): the TAKE line emits `{r} - {v} = {new}` where {new} can be a 2-digit result (e.g. 88-50=38, 38-10=28; 50 distinct 2-digit-result subtractions, v in {10,50}) as one token-span rather than expanded one-digit-per-line. This is a genuine in-weights subtraction, not a copy. Mitigation: it only ever subtracts round values (v in {1,4,5,9,10,40,50,90,100}), is reinforced 7-948x per fact in the corpus, and is the SAME subtraction the deployed legacy reasoner already emits (`remainder {new}`) in a category that never collapsed -> regime-2 LOCAL-DERIVE, acceptable, not an R-killer.

R3 / antipattern-6 (minor): the operator `>=`/`<` plus `take`/`skip` word is a computed magnitude predicate over two literals, not a verbatim copy. Verified single-valued (0 ambiguous (r,v) pairs), so no multimodal continuation; regime-2, acceptable.

R9 (process, not CoT): the 'single structural variable changed vs legacy' claim is overstated -- the redesign couples THREE changes (printed value-table anchor + uniform full-9-row walk + explicit SKIP lines) vs the legacy take-only/skip-rows trace. This muddies clean before/after attribution on the $33 paid run; consider it a 3-variable change for accounting.
